Assert.ok(true, "Ctrl+S in PDF content tab sent PDFJS:Save to the viewer");

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The new Ctrl+S test waits for PDF text-layer rendering and intercepts sendAsyncMessage. It resolves only when that intercepted call is PDFJS:Save, then reaches an unconditional assertion. It deliberately avoids a real download, so it does not assert file contents or a saved path. The override deletes itself on its first invocation; a different first message is forwarded and leaves the local Promise unresolved. Those are static scope and ordering limits, not an observed intermittent failure.
title: The PDF save test observes an actor message rather than a downloaded file
